purpose: Choose the smallest React Bits implementation that earns a product job, then explain rejected alternatives.

components.title: AnimatedList
components.bestFor: A low-frequency list of new results or items entering a visible surface.
components.selectionNote: A hero needs a product promise, not a list reveal.
avoidWhen: live logs or data that changes continuously
the user must scan many rows without movement
components.fallback: Render the list in its final order with a selected or newly-added state.

components.title: BlurText
components.bestFor: A short headline or capability statement that should resolve as the first-view story becomes legible.
components.selectionNote: Use for a short first-view promise, not for long-form reading.
avoidWhen: the text must be available immediately for rapid scanning
components.fallback: Render the headline crisply with no staged blur or delay.

components.title: CountUp
components.bestFor: A meaningful, infrequent number changing as part of a result or success moment.
components.selectionNote: Without a meaningful proof metric, the counter would be decorative.
avoidWhen: live dashboards or frequently refreshing metrics
financial or scientific values users must read exactly
a number is decorative and has no state-change meaning
components.fallback: Show the final value immediately and use a semantic status label.

components.title: FlowingMenu
components.bestFor: An authored, low-frequency navigation or showcase moment where movement explains a visual relationship.
components.selectionNote: It would spend the viewport's signature budget on navigation movement.
avoidWhen: primary product navigation used many times per day
small screens where the moving preview competes with labels
components.fallback: Use a static navigation list with clear active and focus states.

components.title: SpotlightCard
components.bestFor: A secondary proof, capability, or media card that benefits from quiet pointer-led focus.
components.selectionNote: Use as a supporting focus treatment, with a static touch fallback.
avoidWhen: the card is the primary CTA and must stay visually calm
touch-first interaction with no hover equivalent
components.fallback: Use a static surface with border, focus ring, and clear hierarchy.

components.title: TiltedCard
components.bestFor: A visual object or product preview where spatial depth is part of the story.
components.selectionNote: It needs a meaningful visual object and a pointer-friendly surface.
avoidWhen: the surface is touch-first or accessibility-critical
the image is secondary to a text explanation
the product needs a calm, information-dense workspace
components.fallback: Show the media at rest with an optional static caption or overlay.

exampleBriefs.name: ai-product-homepage-hero
why: BlurText gives the short product promise a single first-view reveal.
SpotlightCard gives a secondary proof or capability card quiet focus without adding another signature animation.

reject.AnimatedList-TS-CSS: The hero is not a result list; staggered rows would compete with the product promise.
reject.CountUp-JS-CSS: A metric is not the primary story unless the brief contains a meaningful proof number.
reject.FlowingMenu-JS-CSS: A moving navigation is a stronger signature and would steal attention from the hero message.
reject.TiltedCard-JS-TW: Pointer tilt is less touch-compatible and is unnecessary when the hero has no visual object to inspect.
